--- title: "Phoneme deletion (all positions)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_FONEMAS_TP" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_FONEMAS_TP`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión de fonemas (todas las posiciones)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_FONEMAS_TP.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Phoneme deletion (all positions), from age 6 to 8 (2,137 administrations in 3 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .39. AUC .62–.81 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1940 2009 | | Battery | LEEDUCA and DIS-ESP | | Format | forced choice | | Items | — (1940); 12 (2009) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child repeats a nonsense syllable pronounced by the experimenter, and then, he/she drops the initial or final phoneme. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Revisar el número de ítems. - **2009.** 12 pseudopalabras monosílabas que dice el evaluador; ejemplos orales previos. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![1940 · Supresión de fonemas](../../figuras/plataforma/1940.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1940"} ![2009 · Supresión fonemas](../../figuras/plataforma/2009.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2009"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2009| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 916| 266| 650| 34| | 7.1| 1940| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 554| 189| 364| 31| | 7.1| 1940| 2012| 899|2019/20 | 147| 145| 0| 14| | 8.1| 1940| 2011| 900|2019/20 | 244| 0| 244| 25| | 8.2| 1940| 2010| 639|2018/19 | 276| 78| 198| 25| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 2009| 6.2| 266| 2010| 8.83| 3.65| 10| -1.23| 7.14| 29.70| | 1940| 7.1| 334| 2010, 2012| 7.01| 3.73| 8| -0.47| 8.08| 9.28| | 1940| 8.2| 78| 2010| 8.13| 3.19| 9| -0.69| 3.85| 16.67| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–12 correct responses. | Form| Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----:|----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 2009| 6.2| 266|0–12 |0–12 |0–12 | | | 1940| 7.1| 334|0–12 |0–12 |0–12 | | | 1940| 8.2| 78|0–12 |0–12 |0–12 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .38–.49 (median .39, 3 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .87. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 6.2| 7.1| 499| 0.56| 0.49| | 2010| 6.2| 8.2| 230| 0.42| 0.38| | 2010| 7.1| 8.2| 202| 0.43| 0.39| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .46–.57. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (6.2, r = .59); Word and text reading (7.1, r = .44); Verbal memory (8.1, r = .37); Verbal memory (8.2, r = .34). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .62–.81. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .52–.67. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_FONEMAS_TP_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .69–.81 (4 time points; 224–308 children). ## Provisional norms | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2009| 6.2| 266| 2010| 0| 2| 5| 7| 10| 12| 12| | 1940| 7.1| 334| 2010, 2012| 0| 1| 2| 4| 8| 10| 11| | 1940| 8.1| 244| 2011| 2| 4| 5| 6| 9| 11| 12| | 1940| 8.2| 276| 2010| 3| 4| 6| 7| 9| 11| 12| Each form (platform code) has its own norms, because the forms need not measure on the same scale. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_FONEMAS_TP_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 916| 0.213| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 914| -0.014| 0.838| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 913| 0.013| 0.700| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 916| 0.157| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 677| 0.080| 0.039| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 701| -0.122| 0.108| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 700| -0.073| 0.054| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 701| 0.191| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.1| 243| 0.257| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.1| 244| -0.031| 0.811| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.1| 244| -0.037| 0.565| |School (ICC) | 8.1| 244| 0.147| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.2| 276| 0.224| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.2| 266| 0.076| 0.534| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.2| 266| -0.091| 0.137| |School (ICC) | 8.2| 276| 0.095| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Phoneme deletion (all positions)” (codes 1940 and 2009; LEEDUCA and DIS-ESP battery) assesses phonemic awareness (deletion). The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 12 items. The time limit is 240 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 5 sessions, from 6 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .87 (N = 922, 12 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 8 months) was ρ = .50. Stability across time points was ρ = .38–.49. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .52–.67. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 6.2 (form 2009), 8.2 (form 1940) (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - The task has several forms that never coincide at the same time point: their equivalence cannot be checked; norms are given by form. - La puntuación máxima observada (16) supera el número de ítems (12): puede que se puntúen los ítems de ejemplo, que haya una versión con más ítems o un error de datos. Comprobar antes de describir la tarea y distinguir ítems de prueba y de ejemplo. *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
